source_cards.title: FDN Sandbox: Real-Time Experimentation and Analysis of FDNs
source_cards.bounded_conclusion: FDN Sandbox is useful for inspectable analysis and optimization of the implemented FDN, but its visual metrics, a synthetic-RIR example and average block timings do not establish perceptual preference, measured-room generalization or target-host real-time safety.
methods: actual sfFDN implementation evaluated rather than a differentiable proxy
nine optimization methods including finite-difference gradient and derivative-free methods
colorless objective combines spectral-flatness target 0.56 with sparsity regularization
RIR matching optimizes ten RT60 bands ten tone-correction gains and one global gain using EDR and EDC
limits: flatness target 0.56 is an empirical random-noise heuristic rather than a perceptual threshold
flatness alone can coexist with low echo density
target RIR example is synthetic and no held-out measured-room set is reported
no numeric cross-method RIR-match table or multi-seed convergence analysis
average 128-sample timings on one Intel i9-12900K do not establish p99 p99.9 max xruns allocation-free execution or M3 Max DAW safety

source_cards.title: Shimmer Reverberation with Nonlinear Feedback Delay Networks
source_cards.license_note: paper PDF states CC BY 4.0 while White Rose metadata states CC-BY 2.5; discrepancy retained
source_cards.bounded_conclusion: Nonlinear and time-varying loop operators are credible creative shimmer mechanisms, but approximate energy preservation is not a peak or stability guarantee and the published demonstrations do not validate rock-mix preference, 48-kHz alias control or real-time host safety.
methods: controllable full-wave rectification with first-order antiderivative antialiasing
energy-ratio evaluation on 336 minutes of random MoisesDB stems using 100-ms nonsilent windows
limits: nonlinear spectral redistribution means the intended frequency-dependent T60 is not strictly preserved
CFWR and SDFD show visible aliasing even in the 96-kHz demonstration
DC blocking and adaptive makeup alter low-frequency decay and can add gain modulation
ring modulation and time modification need extra attenuation for short strongly recirculating configurations
ring-buffer and granular methods trade distortion against latency and smearing
no controlled MUSHRA ABX or rock-mix listening test
compute comparison counts mainly multiplications and is not a CPU latency benchmark
companion audio page was unavailable and examples were not reviewed

positive_checks: modular library with unit and performance fixtures
finite and energy-behavior tests present for implemented nonlinear blocks
remaining_gaps: current main implements three of the five paper operators: CFWR SDFD and ring modulation
time-compression and granular implementations were not found
float32 antialias epsilon is 1e-5 rather than the paper's 1e-8
some test dependencies use moving master tags
no musical preference true-peak or target-DAW safety validation

positive_checks: hardening and Debug ASAN configuration are present
a specific sfFDN revision is pinned
remaining_gaps: pinned sfFDN revision 594f85e909081b17da3cb9bb46385419c419f02c differs from current main
no root project license was found; only a ClearSans Apache license file surfaced
app-level automated tests were not found in inspected main
no release artifact or reproduced build
integration blocked pending license clarification and reproducible target-host validation

knowledge_cards.claim: EDR EDC RT60 flatness and echo density are distinct diagnostics and none alone establishes preference.
FDN Sandbox flatness target 0.56 is a study-specific random-noise heuristic rather than a psychoacoustic threshold.
Spectral flatness requires an echo-density or sparsity guard because a sparse tail can still appear spectrally flat.
A synthetic-RIR EDR fit does not establish measured-room generalization or rock-section usefulness.
Mean block time on one CPU does not replace target-host callback tails xruns allocations and multi-instance testing.
A linear FDN target fit must be revalidated after inserting any nonlinear or time-varying loop operator.
Approximate energy preservation is not a sample-peak true-peak BIBO-stability or internal-state guarantee.
DC blockers and adaptive makeup alter low-frequency decay and may add gain modulation.
Nonlinear spectral redistribution prevents strict preservation of a prescribed frequency-dependent T60.
Visible CFWR and SDFD aliasing at 96 kHz requires separate 48-kHz and oversampling or ADAA validation.
Longer pitch-shift periods can reduce distortion while increasing latency and transient smearing.
Implementation subset revision and license constrain applicability: current sfFDN covers three of five methods and the Sandbox application license is unresolved.

revisions: EDR EDC and RT60 match no longer imply perceptual approval.
Approximate energy preservation no longer implies peak safety or universal stability.
A linear FDN target fit must be revalidated after insertion of nonlinear shimmer processing.
Published average CPU timings no longer imply target-host real-time qualification.
Paper-level availability no longer implies that all five operators exist in current sfFDN code.
handoff: Do not treat EDR EDC RT60 agreement or approximate energy preservation as proof of a good or safe reverb. Revalidate decay DC internal sample and true peaks after every nonlinear loop operation on raw renders, and use a separate loudness-matched copy for listening. Nonlinear shimmer remains a section-aware send candidate. Current sfFDN covers three of five paper operators; do not integrate the FDNSandbox application until its project license is clear.
